claims.text: CDC recommended BV regimens: oral metronidazole 500 mg twice daily 7 days, metronidazole 0.75% gel once daily 5 days, clindamycin 2% cream at bedtime 7 days
claims.quote: Metronidazole 500 mg orally 2 times/day for 7 days Metronidazole gel 0.75% one full applicator (5 g) intravaginally, once daily for 5 days Clindamycin cream 2% one full applicator (5 g) intravaginally at bedtime for 7 days

claims.text: Secnidazole, tinidazole and other clindamycin forms are alternative regimens
claims.quote: Alternative regimens include secnidazole oral granules, multiple oral tinidazole regimens, or clindamycin (oral or intravaginal).

claims.text: Secnidazole is an alternative because of higher cost and lack of long-term outcomes
claims.quote: Secnidazole is listed as an alternative regimen, due to its higher cost and lack of long-term outcomes compared with recommended BV treatments.

claims.text: CDC mentions boric acid only for multiple recurrences, as a limited-data option: nitroimidazole 500 mg twice daily 7 days, then boric acid 600 mg daily 21 days, then 0.75% metronidazole gel twice weekly 4 to 6 months (protocol table, summary, FAQ duration, who-table)
claims.quote: for women with multiple recurrences, an oral nitroimidazole (metronidazole or tinidazole 500 mg 2 times/day for 7 days), followed by intravaginal boric acid 600 mg daily for 21 days and suppressive 0.75% metronidazole gel twice weekly for 4–6 months

claims.text: Boric acid is an option for recurrent BV, not a first-episode treatment; not among recommended or alternative regimens
claims.quote: might be an option for women with recurrent BV

claims.text: In the published BV regimens the capsule is used vaginally once daily
claims.quote: followed by intravaginal boric acid 600 mg daily for 21 days

claims.text: Recommended regimens should be used primarily for a first episode
claims.quote: Recommended regimens should be used primarily; alternative regimens can be considered in instances of notable drug allergy or other medical contraindications to the recommended regimens.

claims.text: After a first recurrence, retreatment with the same (or a different) recommended regimen is acceptable
claims.quote: Using a different recommended treatment regimen can be considered for women who have a recurrence; however, retreatment with the same recommended regimen is an acceptable approach for treating persistent or recurrent BV after the first occurrence

claims.text: Suppressive metronidazole gel or 750 mg suppositories twice weekly for more than 3 months reduce recurrences; benefit does not persist after stopping
claims.quote: either 0.75% metronidazole gel or 750 mg metronidazole vaginal suppository twice weekly for >3 months has been reported to reduce recurrences, although this benefit does not persist when suppressive therapy is discontinued

claims.text: CDC does not recommend routine treatment of sex partners
claims.quote: Therefore, routine treatment of sex partners is not recommended.

claims.text: CDC recommends BV treatment for all symptomatic pregnant women, with antibiotic regimens
claims.quote: BV treatment is recommended for all symptomatic pregnant women because symptomatic BV has been associated with adverse pregnancy outcomes

claims.quote: topical boric acid (BA) aimed at biofilm removal was added to nitroimidazole induction and maintenance therapy creating a triple phase regimen

claims.text: Not an FDA-approved drug; prescribed from compounding pharmacies or widely sold OTC, often marketed as homeopathic

claims.text: OTC suppositories marketed for uses from odor and dryness to yeast infections and BV
claims.quote: >20 brands of boric acid (BA)–containing vaginal suppositories, marketed for indications ranging from vaginal odor, discharge, and dryness to VVC, BV, and dyspareunia

claims.text: Powder in a gelatin or vegetable-based capsule; formulations and per-capsule costs vary
claims.quote: Formulations vary; commonly, BA powder is placed in a gelatin or vegetable-based capsule for intravaginal use. Costs online range from $0.10 to $1.20 per capsule; costs at 2 compounding pharmacies were $0.19 to $2.33 per capsule.

claims.text: Usually 600 mg
claims.quote: Most described 600 mg once daily or BID for 7 to 14 days

claims.text: Boric acid (H3BO3) is a borate compound formed when boron combines with oxygen
claims.quote: BA (H3BO3) is a borate compound resulting when boron combines with oxygen.

claims.text: Much poisoning data involves accidental or purposeful swallowing of insecticides or cleaning products, often by children
claims.quote: Much of acute human toxicity data relates to case series of reported accidental or purposeful oral ingestion, often in children, of BA-containing insecticides or cleaning products.

claims.text: Swallowed boric acid is almost completely absorbed
claims.quote: Orally ingested BA seems to be nearly 100% systemically absorbed, although quickly renally excreted.

claims.text: Appears safe at commonly prescribed vaginal doses
claims.quote: available data suggest IBA use is safe, at least when used in doses commonly described in the literature as being prescribed by clinicians

claims.text: Safety data are sparse
claims.quote: IBA is not a Food and Drug Administration-approved drug, and safety data are sparse.

claims.text: Few data on longer-term or suppressive regimens
claims.quote: Few data on the safety of longer-term or suppressive regimens prescribed are available, although significant toxicities have not been reported

claims.text: Documented adverse events since 1888 sporadic and mild, mainly local irritation or watery discharge
claims.quote: Since 1888, the only other documented adverse events have been sporadic and mild, primarily limited to local irritation or watery vaginal discharge

claims.text: Mechanism of action uncertain, under investigation
claims.quote: mechanisms of action are uncertain, although under investigation

claims.text: 600 mg dose never tested in dose-range studies
claims.quote: no dose-range studies to evaluate safety or efficacy have ever been performed

claims.text: Guidelines recommend avoiding boric acid in pregnancy; data insufficient to change that
claims.quote: Information on harms in pregnancy is limited, and data remain insufficient to change current guidelines, which recommend IBA avoidance in pregnancy.

claims.text: One human study and less clearly a second raised concern about birth defects
claims.quote: Data from one and less clearly a second human study have raised concerns regarding the teratogenic potential of IBA.

claims.text: The safety assessment is a narrative review
claims.quote: Data on Safety of Intravaginal Boric Acid Use in Pregnant and Nonpregnant Women: A Narrative Review.
